blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Life & Annuities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Life books run on decades-long promises: underwriting quality at issue, servicing responsiveness across 30-year relationships, and actuarial integrity across regime changes (IFRS 17/LDTI). The machinery deciding those outcomes is data and document heavy — ideal ground for governed automation.

items: Underwriting health data and beneficiary PII create long-retention sensitive estates; PQ exposure deep.
APS records, paramedical data and financial underwriting arrive as documents; assembly consumes days per case.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery, Identity & Access Modernization, Identity & Access Modernization from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Underwriting evidence assembly, Policy servicing transactions, Claims/beneficiary processing) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — IFRS 17 / LDTI among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Classification-aware controls for health/PII archives (sensitive estate governed)

blocks.caption: Regimes shaping this capability
rows: reserving, capital and model governance under supervisory review

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: classification-aware DLP, encryption policy and access analytics across health/financial stores (breach-surface measurable and shrinking). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
